summary: Édouard Specht was a sinologist who studied under Jean-Pierre-Guillaume Pauthier and Stanislas Julien. In 1892, he held a post teaching Chinese at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Édouard-Simon Ariel was an Indologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf from 1840 to 1844. In 1846, he served as Conservator at the Bibliothèque publique de Pondichéry.
Élisée Reclus studied at the Faculté libre de théologie protestante de Montauban from 1848 to 1849. He later held a post at the New University of Brussels from circa 1894 to 1905.

Émile Benveniste was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of Paris, he studied under Antoine Meillet, Joseph Vendryes, Sylvain Lévi, and Louis Finot, later serving at EPHE and Collège de France.

Émile Boisacq was a linguist who studied at the Université libre de Bruxelles, Heidelberg University, and the University of Paris under Hermann Osthoff, Ludwig Sütterlin, Michel Bréal, Victor Henry, and Antoine Meillet. He served as professor at ULB (1895–1935).
Émile Bréhier was a philosopher who studied at the University of Paris under Henri Bergson. He later held a post at the University of Paris from circa 1919 to 1946.
Émile Chartier was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Pierre-Corneille (circa 1881–1886) and École Normale Supérieure (circa 1889–1892).

Émile Chatelain was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (circa 1874–1876), he held posts at the École française de Rome (1876–1877) and the EPHE (circa 1882–1933).

Émile Durkheim worked in philosophy and religious studies. Educated at ENS and Leipzig under Wilhelm Wundt, he held posts at the University of Bordeaux (1887–1902), the Sorbonne (circa 1902–1917), the University of Paris, and EPHE.
Émile Littré worked in linguistics and philosophy. He studied at the Lycée Louis-le-Grand from circa 1815 to 1819 and at the Paris Medical Faculty from circa 1822 to 1830.

Émile Senart was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology who studied under Martin Haug at Munich and Theodor Benfey at Göttingen. He served as president of the Société Asiatique (1908–1928) and as a professor at the Collège de France.

Émile-Louis Burnouf worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf, at ENS, and at the University of Paris. He was a professor at Nancy (1854–1867) and director of the École française d'Athènes (1867–1875).

Émilie Aussant works in Indology and linguistics. Having studied under Georges-Jean Pinault, she held a post at Paris Diderot University (attested 2014) and became a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 2022.

Étienne Balazs was a sinologist and historian who studied under Otto Franke from 1923 to 1930. He held posts at the CNRS (1949) and as a professor of Chinese economic history at the University of Paris (circa 1949–1963).

Étienne Lamotte was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at KU Leuven, Sapienza, and Paris under Louis de La Vallée Poussin and Sylvain Lévi, among others, he served at KU Leuven (1932–1974) and Université catholique de Louvain (1950–1959).

Étienne Marc Quatremère studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. Active in linguistics, history, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held professorships at Rouen (circa 1809–1819), Collège de France (1819–1857), and INALCO (1827–1857).

Ñāṇamoli Thera was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Exeter College, Oxford (circa 1924–1928), and subsequently under traditional teachers Nyanatiloka Mahathera (1949) and Palane Vajiranana (1950).

Óscar Cortés is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied philosophy at the University of Guadalajara (2007–2013) and earned a master's at El Colegio de México (2015–2017), later working as a researcher at Palabra de Clío (2018–2020).

Ösel Tendzin was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Fordham University and under Satchidananda Saraswati and Chögyam Trungpa. He was named executive vice president of Vajradhatu in 1973 and succeeded Trungpa in 1987.

Ülo Valk is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Tartu (circa 1981–1986), he held a post there around 1995 and served as an editor for Numen from circa 2014 to 2018.
